facts.activity_file: maintaining portable and mobile extinguishing equipment

assets.label: export transfer pumps
assets.service: tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family

control_failures.control_label: provision and briefing of a competent fire watch
alarm, muster and accounting for people
standby attendance and non-entry rescue capability

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: stored energy found after isolation of P-7110

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control FIRE_WATCH_PROVISION: the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control MUSTER_AND_ACCOUNTING: the alarm, muster and accounting for people was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control STANDBY_ATTENDANCE_AND_RESCUE: the standby attendance and non-entry rescue capability was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the standby attendance and non-entry rescue capability on P-7110, PT-7110 and TK-7101 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining fire protection systems, specifically maintaining portable and mobile extinguishing equipment. P-7110 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was not in place. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 15 August 2013 a hazard report was recorded on P-7110, PT-7110 and TK-7101 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
